skills.name: Narrow AI and General AI
skills.learning_objective: Distinguish between narrow artificial intelligence and artificial general intelligence.

intents.description: Select the statement that correctly defines narrow AI (competence limited to one task) as distinct from artificial general intelligence (human-like breadth across tasks).
intents.justification: direct recognition of a defined concept

intents.description: Given a system description, classify it as narrow AI (single-task competence) or artificial general intelligence (human-like breadth).
Given two system descriptions, compare their scope of competence and identify which is narrow AI and which is (claimed) artificial general intelligence.

skills.name: Real-world AI systems
skills.learning_objective: Identify appropriate applications of AI in different fields.

intents.description: Given one clear real-world scenario, identify the single AI subfield or technique it exemplifies (e.g. search, ML, NLP, vision).
Given a scenario combining several plausible AI application areas, select the one that is the best fit and explain why the others are less appropriate.
intents.justification: multi-step application requiring several components at once

skills.name: Machine intelligence
skills.learning_objective: Explain how the Turing Test and Chinese Room argument relate to machine intelligence and understanding.

intents.description: Select the statement that correctly defines what the Turing Test measures, as distinct from what the Chinese Room argument challenges.
intents.justification: direct recognition of a defined concept

intents.description: Given a description of the Turing Test or the Chinese Room argument, identify what it claims to test or demonstrate.

Compare the claim the Turing Test makes about machine intelligence (behavioural indistinguishability) with the objection the Chinese Room argument raises against that claim (behaviour without understanding).
